title: Release notes
intro: Newest first. The first public day is 28 August 2026 (the website). The Unreal project starts 4 September. There is no 28 September note — that date has not happened. Empty calendar days are listed so a quiet week is not a missing week.

items.title: AFTERLIGHT is the public game name
items.body: Volume One of the story is on the site (9,489 words, EPUB). Afterlight radio plays on demand. The homepage leads with the Puerto Rico campaign. Training stays a chapter of the game, request-only. No public demo button.
items.canExperience: Read Volume One. Play the site radio. Request access for the range.
items.inDevelopment: Playable campaign island, public demo, in-game radios as unlocks.

items.title: Internal range beta candidate
items.body: An internal Windows range candidate exists for studio play. First-bullet credit is the rule on that lane. Hangar and sky are still held. This is not a public demo.
items.inDevelopment: Human-play public demo, hangar finish, campaign.

items.title: No public landing
items.body: No website or game commit this calendar day. Work from the 15th and 17th still stands.

items.title: Hangar polish, still internal
items.body: Tip-only hangar declutter and impact-rim polish on the internal shipping range. Sign-off stays in the studio. Not a public build.
items.canExperience: Request-only range if you already have a yes.

items.title: Hangar and dummy presentation
items.body: Internal shipping-style range drops: clearer impacts, less clutter in the hangar, combat dummy presentation. Studio packages, not Steam.
items.canExperience: Request-only range if you already have a yes.

items.title: Hardware lighting path and range structure
items.body: Packaged range work: hangar floor edges, observation tower, native 12 m head kept live in the micro-correction mode. Hardware lighting path for RTX machines. Internal.

items.title: No public landing
items.body: No game or site commit this calendar day.

items.title: The site tells the lab clearly
items.body: First website commits since 28 August. Homepage uses a range still. Support via Ko-fi. Development catalog published. The quiet stretch on dtrtlab.com was not idle: the Unreal range was moving in the game repo from 4 September.
items.canExperience: The public site, including how to request access.

items.title: Kestrel and the lane get real materials
items.body: Original Kestrel viewmodel (hands, rails, optic, PBR). Range backstop, crates, clouds. Command-center home in the build. Still no public installer.
items.canExperience: Website only, unless Ian already granted a build.
items.inDevelopment: Everything players would call a game besides the lane.

items.title: Menus, results, range light
items.body: Production menus, session lifecycle, persistent results. Range palette and barrel orientation fixes. Fast trigger taps keep timestamps. Internal.

items.title: No public landing
items.body: No game or site commit this calendar day (Monday after the 6–7 range burst).

items.title: Keep the lane on screen
items.body: Visual dressing that went black is turned off so the range stays visible.

items.title: Lobby, settings, honest shots
items.body: A simple lobby and mouse/FOV settings. Each shot can retrigger fire sound. Walking heads do not count.

items.title: A named 12 m lane
items.body: The range gets a clear 12-metre purpose: acquire, still, first bullet. Session score and reset exist in the build.
items.inDevelopment: Look of the hangar, public access, campaign.

items.title: The Windows range begins
items.body: The official Unreal project starts this day. First-person range, Kestrel rifle, 1:1 mouse look. Internal. The public website from 28 August is unchanged.
items.canExperience: Nothing public to play. The site is still the only public surface.
items.inDevelopment: The range, credit law, and everything else.

items.title: Quiet week — no game repo yet
items.body: 29 August through 3 September: no dtrtlab.com commits and no Unreal repository. The site from 28 August stays up. Game engineering starts 4 September. This is not a missing September 28 entry.
items.inDevelopment: The Unreal game, which does not exist on disk yet.

items.title: The lab site opens
items.body: Friday 28 August 2026. dtrtlab.com goes live. Contact, FAQ, and legal pages. There is no game download.
